this month. Russia's health authorities say no cases of plague have been detected among
workers at a Siberian infectious diseases laboratory where a technician died under mysterious
circumstances last week. The case has prompted global concern over an outbreak of the plague
or some other pathogen, as NPR's Charles Maynes reports.
Russia's consumer health watchdog, Rospatreb Nazor, has already insisted the death of a
female lab technician at an anti-plague research facility in Russia's Irkutsk region was due
to a form of pneumonia. Now, a subsequent investigation finds no pathogens linked to
her work in her body, a claim Rospatreb Nazor said extended to other workers the woman had
contact with. Separately, Russian authorities formally told the World Health Organization
there were no cases of plague in Irkutsk. Under global health rules, Russia is required

Charles Maynes, NPR News, Moscow.
